rows.name: Coinbase Bridge
farm_steps: Use a fresh wallet that holds only the funds you plan to farm Coinbase Bridge with, and keep its seed phrase offline. Cost: under $5 of gas for the first transaction on Bitcoin. Time: 5 minutes.

Open Coinbase Bridge's own site from its official listing, check for a points or rewards page, and note what it counts before you deposit anything. Cost: nothing to read, and never pay anyone to be whitelisted. Time: 20 minutes.
Bridge $250 of USDC to Bitcoin through Coinbase Bridge and use the bridged funds in its app. Cost: $250 of capital and about $3 of gas on Bitcoin. Time: 15 minutes to set up.

Bridge a second, smaller amount back through Coinbase Bridge so the wallet shows traffic in both directions. Cost: about $3 of gas on Bitcoin, with no new capital. Time: 10 minutes, in the second week.

Repeat one qualifying action on Coinbase Bridge every week, such as a deposit, a borrow, a swap or a vote, always from the same wallet. Cost: about $3 of gas a week on Bitcoin. Time: 10 minutes a week.
Hold the position for at least 30 days so the activity is counted in more than one weekly snapshot. Cost: the $250 stays in the position for the whole hold. Time: 30 days.

Keep a farm log with the wallet, the dates and every transaction hash, and claim any reward only from the link Coinbase Bridge itself publishes. Cost: nothing but the log, and never a fee to claim. Time: 5 minutes a week, 15 minutes to unwind at the end.

Open Keyrock's own site from its official listing, check for a points or rewards page, and note what it counts before you deposit anything. Cost: nothing to read, and never pay anyone to be whitelisted. Time: 20 minutes.
Deposit $50 into a Keyrock vault on Arc and keep the shares. Cost: $50 of capital and about $3 of gas on Arc. Time: 15 minutes to set up.
Add a second, smaller deposit to the same Keyrock vault in a later week. Cost: about $3 of gas on Arc, with no new capital. Time: 10 minutes, in the second week.
Repeat one qualifying action on Keyrock every week, such as a deposit, a borrow, a swap or a vote, always from the same wallet. Cost: about $3 of gas a week on Arc. Time: 10 minutes a week.
Hold the position for at least 60 days so the activity is counted in more than one weekly snapshot. Cost: the $50 stays in the position for the whole hold. Time: 60 days.

Keep a farm log with the wallet, the dates and every transaction hash, and claim any reward only from the link Keyrock itself publishes. Cost: nothing but the log, and never a fee to claim. Time: 5 minutes a week, 15 minutes to unwind at the end.

Open Exponent Yield Exchange's own site from its official listing, check for a points or rewards page, and note what it counts before you deposit anything. Cost: nothing to read, and never pay anyone to be whitelisted. Time: 20 minutes.
Provide $50 of liquidity to Exponent Yield Exchange's main pool on Solana and keep the position open. Cost: $50 of capital and about $1 of gas on Solana. Time: 15 minutes to set up.

Make one swap through Exponent Yield Exchange's own interface on Solana so the wallet records both trading and liquidity activity. Cost: about $1 of gas on Solana, with no new capital. Time: 10 minutes, in the second week.

Repeat one qualifying action on Exponent Yield Exchange every week, such as a deposit, a borrow, a swap or a vote, always from the same wallet. Cost: about $1 of gas a week on Solana. Time: 10 minutes a week.
Hold the position for at least 30 days so the activity is counted in more than one weekly snapshot. Cost: the $50 stays in the position for the whole hold. Time: 30 days.

Keep a farm log with the wallet, the dates and every transaction hash, and claim any reward only from the link Exponent Yield Exchange itself publishes. Cost: nothing but the log, and never a fee to claim. Time: 5 minutes a week, 15 minutes to unwind at the end.

Open Plasma One's own site from its official listing, check for a points or rewards page, and note what it counts before you deposit anything. Cost: nothing to read, and never pay anyone to be whitelisted. Time: 20 minutes.
Deposit $50 of USDC into Plasma One on Plasma and keep the position open. Cost: $50 of capital and about $3 of gas on Plasma. Time: 15 minutes to set up.
Make one more deposit or swap inside Plasma One on Plasma in a later week, from the same wallet. Cost: about $3 of gas on Plasma, with no new capital. Time: 10 minutes, in the second week.
Repeat one qualifying action on Plasma One every week, such as a deposit, a borrow, a swap or a vote, always from the same wallet. Cost: about $3 of gas a week on Plasma. Time: 10 minutes a week.
Hold the position for at least 30 days so the activity is counted in more than one weekly snapshot. Cost: the $50 stays in the position for the whole hold. Time: 30 days.

Keep a farm log with the wallet, the dates and every transaction hash, and claim any reward only from the link Plasma One itself publishes. Cost: nothing but the log, and never a fee to claim. Time: 5 minutes a week, 15 minutes to unwind at the end.

Supply $50 of USDC to marginfi Lending on Solana and keep the position open. Cost: $50 of capital and about $1 of gas on Solana. Time: 15 minutes to set up.

Borrow a small amount against the supply on marginfi Lending, repay it a week later, and keep the supply in place. Cost: about $1 of gas on Solana, with no new capital. Time: 10 minutes, in the second week.

Repeat one qualifying action on marginfi Lending every week, such as a deposit, a borrow, a swap or a vote, always from the same wallet. Cost: about $1 of gas a week on Solana. Time: 10 minutes a week.
Hold the position for at least 30 days so the activity is counted in more than one weekly snapshot. Cost: the $50 stays in the position for the whole hold. Time: 30 days.

Keep a farm log with the wallet, the dates and every transaction hash, and claim any reward only from the link marginfi Lending itself publishes. Cost: nothing but the log, and never a fee to claim. Time: 5 minutes a week, 15 minutes to unwind at the end.
